race_context: The district: Clay Community Schools, based in Brazil, serves parts of Clay and Parke counties; Ballotpedia reports 4,114 students in 10 schools in the 2023-24 school year {bp_clay}. The district lists ten schools, including Northview High School and Clay City Jr./Sr. High School {ccs_supt}. Dr. Brady Scott, formerly assistant superintendent, is superintendent; the board considered his contract, starting July 1, 2026 with a $187,000 base salary, in May 2026 after Dr. Tim Rayle announced his retirement {ccs_supt}{bt_scott}.

The board has seven members serving four-year terms {bp_clay}. Four members are elected from districts 1–4, which were on the ballot in November 2024, and three are elected at large, last chosen in November 2022 {bp_clay_elections}{bt_2024_results}{clay_2022_results}. Current members are Tom Reberger (president), Dr. Michael Shaw (vice president), Charley Jackson (secretary), Amy Burke Adams (assistant secretary), Andrea Baysinger, Dr. David Bess and Cheryl Schopmeyer {ccs_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three at-large seats, so voters may choose up to three, not one as shown on the state list {bt_filing}{bp_clay_elections}{in_list}. The seats are held by Cheryl Schopmeyer, Amy Burke Adams and Charley Jackson, and all three are running again {bt_filing}. Schopmeyer and Burke Adams won at-large seats in 2022; Jackson finished fifth in that race and joined the board later (Ballotpedia lists him as taking office in 2024) {clay_2022_results}{bp_clay}.

Party labels: this is the first Indiana school board election in which candidates may list a party under Public Law 195 (formerly Senate Bill 287); the Clay County Election Office reported that Mike Ames filed as an Independent and the other six as Republicans {bt_filing}.

Budget and taxes (2026): at a May 2026 meeting, Board President Tom Reberger said bonds were being issued for capital projects ahead of a statewide restructuring of school funds, and member Dr. David Bess noted that other districts were turning to tax referendums {bt_scott}. At the Sept. 10, 2026 meeting, Szabo, who presented financial items to the board, said he anticipated a tax rate of about 88 cents per $100 of assessed value {bt_sept_meeting}.

Transportation (2026): the board held a public hearing on Sept. 10, 2026 on an amended bus replacement plan, after Reberger raised concerns about interest and depreciation tied to seven spare buses; the district posted a call for bus drivers two days earlier {bt_forum}.

Facilities (May 2026): the board heard estimates for North Clay gym floor work ($38,000–$275,000) and possible artificial turf baseball and softball fields at Northview and Clay City (up to $1.5 million for a full baseball field); Jackson said he requested the presentation after spring rainouts, and Burke Adams asked about the timing given expected funding challenges {bt_scott}.

Academics and accountability (2026): in April 2026 Scott briefed the board on Indiana's new A–F school grading model, with 2025-26 as a 'year zero', and said attendance policies were being tightened {bt_grades}. The district reported a 96.9% IREAD pass rate for 2026 {bt_sept_meeting}. The board is carrying out a 2026–2031 Academic Strategic Plan {bt_forum}.

Forums: the Brazil Public Library and The Brazil Times held a candidate forum on Sept. 24, 2026 with reader-submitted questions {bt_forum_notice}{bt_forum}. Six candidates attended; Jackson did not {bt_forum}. Main differences there: Burke Adams said the district was not discussing staff cuts or school closings and backed its one-to-one Chromebook program, while most other candidates called for limits on classroom device use; Rickert proposed reviewing administrator pay, Crafton raised replacing property taxes with other taxes, Ames and Karn Clodfelter called for changes to public comment at board meetings {bt_forum}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large member and board assistant secretary, first elected in 2022 {clay_2022_results}{ccs_board}.
background: Won an at-large seat in November 2022 with 2,857 votes, third among eight candidates for three seats {clay_2022_results}.
At the 2026 forum said she had attended an estimated 48 graduations {bt_forum}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for an at-large seat by the June 18, 2026 deadline and is running as a Republican, according to the Clay County Election Office {bt_filing}{in_list}.

items: Said at the Sept. 24, 2026 forum: 'We are not discussing reducing staff or closing schools,' pointing to energy savings from lighting and fuel-bank participation, and added, 'We're in better shape than those around us' {bt_forum}.
Described academic achievement, measured by results such as IREAD scores, as both the mission of the 2026–2031 Academic Strategic Plan and a measure of the curriculum team's work {bt_forum}.

Was the only forum candidate fully in favor of the district's current Chromebook use, saying she supported the K–12 one-to-one device program and that 'Traditional teaching instruction still takes place' {bt_forum}.
Said artificial intelligence would never replace teachers, and noted that a policy guidance provider using AI was replaced with a human-based service after errors were found {bt_forum}.
Said she supports the bus replacement plans and cited the new bus center among facility upgrades during her tenure {bt_forum}.
At a May 2026 meeting asked about the reasoning behind considering artificial turf fields in light of possible funding challenges for public schools {bt_scott}.
Said board members are 'out and about' and pointed to community surveys the district has conducted; 'I show up,' she said {bt_forum}.
Noted that the district restricted cell phones before Indiana's statewide ban {bt_forum}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. At the 2026 forum she described the district's finances as stronger than neighboring districts' and cited the new bus center and the cell phone restrictions as board actions {bt_forum}.
